Executive summary

Bottom line (ELI5): This project has built and used real receiver-side collection infrastructure. It can create named, replayable two-channel IQ packages with independent ADS-B context. The remaining work is to prove that the physical reference chain and collection controls are trustworthy enough for field promotion—not to claim that aircraft measurements already exist.

What was built

Rooftop RF observation hardware, enclosure/cabling, a dual-channel N320 capture path, a capture workstation, and independent ADS-B/GPS support. PH-001–PH-008

What is demonstrated

Physical deployment, coordinated historical packages, package recovery, G1 replayability, and saved-baseline digital alignment. PKG-001; SYNC-001

What remains unresolved

Reference-path adequacy, field channel-role verification, lock/drop evidence, and collection-suitability approval. RF-002; CTRL-001

Why it matters

The next experiment starts from an installed, reviewable evidence chain rather than a one-off rooftop setup or undocumented workstation state.

What should happen next

Run the controlled 599 MHz / 6.144 MS/s / 0 Hz field baseline with immutable roles, explicit readbacks, lock/drop records, and a PASS/HOLD decision. CTRL-001

1. Purpose and current status

Bottom line (ELI5): The project has built more than an idea for a passive radar. It has a receiver-side installation, a dual-channel recording path, an ADS-B collection path, named session packages, and a way to replay saved data. Those are meaningful accomplishments. They do not yet prove that the system detects, tracks, or localizes aircraft.

This report explains the physical collection system that sits before later processing and G4-R work. It treats a collection as an evidence package: raw dual-channel IQ, independent ADS-B records, capture logs, configuration/readback metadata, and a session manifest should travel together. The report separates what is photographed, implemented, or demonstrated on a named recording from what the next field-readiness sequence still has to prove.

The strongest current conclusion is therefore infrastructure exists and has been used to create reviewable historical packages. The responsible conclusion is not “ready for operational collection.” Reference-chain adequacy, controlled channel-role confirmation, explicit hardware state, and collection-suitability acceptance remain open.

2. Why collection infrastructure matters

Bottom line (ELI5): Later signal processing can only be trusted if it can answer a simple question: “What exactly was recorded, when, with which hardware, and how can we check it again?” Collection infrastructure is what makes that question answerable.

Passive bistatic processing compares two recordings of an existing HDTV broadcast. A reference path is intended to receive a direct copy of the broadcast; a surveillance path is intended to observe the scene containing the direct signal plus possible reflections. Both are sampled by the same dual-channel receiver. ADS-B is collected independently so it can supply post-hoc aircraft/geometry context rather than steering the raw IQ capture or later detector decisions.

That architecture turns a radio recording into a reviewable experiment. The physical deployment creates repeatable RF access. The coordinator starts and stops related processes with a shared session ID. The package preserves the artifacts that later analysis needs. The replay path lets the team check a claimed result without reconnecting the rooftop hardware.

Important boundary: a visible antenna, a completed IQ file, or an ADS-B log is not a radar-performance result. It is evidence that a prerequisite collection capability exists. Aircraft detection, tracking, localization, operational probability of detection (Pd), and operational false-alarm rate (Pfa) require separately validated downstream evidence.

Primary evidence: S02 system and coordinated-capture orientation, PassiveBistaticRestart gate terminology, and truth-separation decision.

3. System overview and hardware architecture

Bottom line (ELI5): The transmitter is not built by this project—it is an existing HDTV broadcaster. The project built the receiver-side infrastructure: two observation paths into one N320, a capture computer, and a separate ADS-B/GPS collection path that helps explain what was happening during a recording.

The documented hardware inventory comprises a USRP N320 dual-channel software-defined radio, a directional HDTV/Yagi surveillance antenna, a direct-path/reference antenna configuration, a collection computer/rack, rooftop enclosure and conduit, a Raspberry Pi-based ADS-B/GPS collection subsystem, RTL-SDR hardware for ADS-B support, and a GPS HAT/PPS timekeeping component. The N320 hardware exposes external reference/PPS interfaces; the repository also contains GPS/NMEA logging that records system time and chrony information. Those facts establish available infrastructure, not a demonstrated end-to-end reference-lock or PPS-discipline record for a flight collection.

For the current/recovery baseline, the documented intended mapping is RF0:RX2 → channel 1 → surveillance and RF1:RX2 → channel 2 → reference. That mapping must be captured and verified physically; signal-power ranking is explicitly not a valid substitute. The August antenna-comparison interpretation is under correction because its original changed/control role assignment was reversed.

5. How a collection happens

Bottom line (ELI5): A good collection is coordinated rather than improvised. One shared session ID ties together the IQ recording, the ADS-B window, the machine logs, and the manifest that tells a later reviewer where everything went.

The implemented shell coordinator performs five practical jobs: verify SSH access to the Raspberry Pi; launch the session-named ADS-B logger; wait a configured lead time; call MATLAB to make the N320 IQ capture; then keep ADS-B running through a tail interval, stop it gracefully, fetch outputs, and package them locally. The local MATLAB wrapper passes the session ID into the N320 logging path, gathers written IQ files, and reads available baseband-header metadata such as recording time, center frequency, sample rate, and LO offset.

GPS/NMEA logging is a separate implemented support path. Its logger connects to gpsd, retains NMEA sentences, and writes periodic system-time and chrony-statistics records. The historical manifests examined for this report package ADS-B truth, not NMEA; therefore GPS should be described as available collection infrastructure, not assumed session evidence.

Primary evidence: S03 shell coordinator, S04 local capture/readback wrapper, S06 ADS-B logger, and S06 NMEA logger.

5A. Installed cueing and time infrastructure (added in V5)

Bottom line (ELI5): The ADS-B Raspberry Pi now also runs a service that tells the collection desktop, over the data network, which aircraft could be worth collecting on. Collections are still started by hand. Setting it up also showed that the Pi’s clock, which timestamps the ADS-B truth, had been about 15 seconds slow; it now keeps time from internet NTP, which the owner has accepted.

The ADS-B Cue Tasker runs on the same Raspberry Pi as dump1090 and the ADS-B/GPS loggers, as the systemd service adsb-cue (headless adsb-console, enabled at boot, restarted by systemd if dump1090 is not yet up). It publishes one compressed JSON message per UDP datagram to the multicast group 239.192.10.1:31986 with TTL 1, so only hosts on the rooftop data network receive it. Its observer configuration holds only the real receive site. On the collection desktop the MATLAB CueListener receives and ranks the cues; it does not start captures, and the coordinated capture workflow in section 5 is unchanged. CUE-001

The architecture designs the Pi as a stratum-0 time source with GPS and 1-PPS. As built on 2026-09-26, chrony on the Pi keeps time from internet NTP through a NAT on the collection desktop; the GPS/PPS reference clocks are configured but not locked. The owner accepted internet NTP as the time source on 2026-09-26, with a stated tolerance of 0.1 s between the Pi and the collection desktop (proposed from the one check, +0.05 to +0.09 s). GPS/PPS lock is a hardware to-do (a loose component is suspected), not a blocker for NTP-based timing. On 2026-09-25, before the NTP route existed, the Pi was measured 14.9 s slow with chrony unsynchronised. The N320 capture timestamps come from the desktop’s NTP clock, while the ADS-B records are timestamped on the Pi, so an error in the Pi clock is an error in the IQ-to-ADS-B alignment. TIME-001

6. Session packaging and provenance

Bottom line (ELI5): The historical session manifest is the collection’s packing list. It does not contain the radio samples themselves, but it names the session, records the requested and observed capture settings, and points to radar, ADS-B, and log artifacts.

The established package layout is captures/<session_id>/radar/, truth/, logs/, and session_manifest.json. Two August 27 example manifests show the pattern operating on real sessions. Each records a UTC session ID, capture duration/repetitions, lead and tail intervals, N320 requested settings, header readback, a radar-file list, compressed ADS-B artifact(s), and local/Pi log paths. The examples record 15 one-second parts at 599 MHz, 6.144 MS/s, and zero LO offset—not a one-file production collection.

That is useful provenance, but it is not yet the complete future field-evidence chain. The historical examples do not explicitly record channel roles, antenna/cable identity, radio lock state, dropped/overflow count, file hashes, or NMEA/GPS paths. The current hardware-readiness plan correctly identifies those omissions as fields that must be recorded and accepted rather than inferred.

Physical evidence

The photographed capture station, receiver enclosure, and cabling provide the tangible collection environment from which the named package was produced.

Quantitative evidence

The sampled manifest records 15 IQ parts, one ADS-B gzip artifact, two logs, 599 MHz, 6.144 MS/s, and matching readback fields.

Engineering interpretation

The package has enough evidence to replay and challenge a saved session, but not enough to certify the field hardware configuration that produced it.

7. What now exists that did not exist before this project

Bottom line (ELI5): The durable value is an instrumented collection capability: hardware at the site, software that coordinates a session, independent ADS-B context, packages that can be reopened, and analysis gates that can challenge the data. That is infrastructure value, even before a radar-performance claim is justified.

The assets below are deliberately written as infrastructure accomplishments. They are not converted into detector, tracker, localization, Pd, or Pfa claims. The project has reduced the cost of the next experiment by making physical setup, raw data, metadata, session packaging, and replay more repeatable and reviewable.

Physical evidence

The receiver site, enclosure labels, cabling, and capture station survive as real project assets rather than a slide-only concept.

Quantitative evidence

Named manifests, G1's 18/18 artifact reconciliation, and G3's saved-baseline metrics show that the assets have produced inspectable digital evidence.

Engineering interpretation

The lasting capability is repeatable experimentation with a traceable evidence chain. Field qualification and radar-performance claims remain separate next steps.

8. What evidence shows the hardware and workflow work?

Bottom line (ELI5): The evidence is not an activity list. It is a chain: physical photographs show installed assets; manifests show named session packages; file-header readbacks show that capture metadata can be recovered; G1 shows a saved session can be decoded and replayed; and G3 shows that recorded channels can be digitally aligned on that baseline.

Commissioning and installation evidence. The rooftop and stairwell photographs establish that the support structures, cable routing, enclosure, collection rack, and antenna mounting work were physically performed. This matters because it turns future experiments into configuration-control work rather than a fresh installation project.

Collection artifact evidence. The two August 27 manifests name five historical sessions and show 15-part IQ collections with associated ADS-B gzip files and logs. The two examples examined here record matching requested and header-readback values for 599 MHz, 6.144 MS/s, and zero LO offset. The manifests therefore support a narrow but useful claim: the coordinated workflow produced recoverable session records with IQ and ADS-B artifacts.

Readback and replay evidence. The local capture wrapper prints the session ID, produced files, recording time, and available baseband-header readback. On the frozen reference session, G1 reported 18/18 required manifest artifacts, a 6144000 × 2 complex-int16 decode contract per one-second file, and 14 checked seams. G3 then reported zero-sample maximum lag spread, 0.019 Hz median absolute residual frequency, and coherent short/medium/long review windows. These are bounded data/replay results, not field acceptance of the RF chain.

9. Current collection limitations

Bottom line (ELI5): The project can collect and replay data, but it cannot yet call a collection field-qualified. The main uncertainty is not whether software exists; it is whether the recorded hardware state, reference chain, role mapping, and collection integrity have been proven in the field.

The most important limitations are evidence gaps that change the permitted claim. They should be closed with controlled checks and recorded readbacks, not papered over with power-based guesses or favorable downstream plots.

Channel Role Verification Evidence

Current supporting evidence

  • PH-004 photographs labels inside the receiver enclosure: RF0 is marked surveillance and RF1 reference.
  • CTRL-001 defines the canonical mapping: RF0:RX2 → channel 1 → Surveillance Path; RF1:RX2 → channel 2 → Reference Path.
  • RF-002 used this mapping manually for role-aware diagnostic review, while retaining the provenance caveat.

Missing evidence and closure test

  • The historical manifests do not store ordered physical ports, semantic roles, antenna/cable identities, or a field role-verification result.
  • Close the issue with labeled/photographed connectors, a controlled disconnect or injected-stimulus test, ordered manifest fields, and a retained field log signed into the package.
  • Under CTRL-001, keep RF0 fixed and change only RF1 during the A-B-A reference-chain experiment.

Channel Role Assignment Boundary

The current RF0/RF1 role interpretation is supported by installation and control evidence but is not yet encoded in the historical manifest schema and therefore remains an analyst-supported assignment rather than a manifest-proven fact.

  • Supports the assignment: PH-004 visibly labels the enclosure-side paths as RF0 surveillance and RF1 reference; CTRL-001 records the same canonical port/channel/role mapping for future controlled collection. CTRL-001 is a proposed control plan, not executed field proof.
  • Observational evidence only: RF-002 applied the declared mapping manually and found the Reference Path 9.969 dB below the Surveillance Path in the saved baseline. That IQ-power observation diagnoses path behavior; it does not identify physical channel roles.
  • Still missing: the historical manifests omit ordered ports, semantic roles, antenna/cable identity, and a retained controlled role-verification result.
  • Why power-based swapping is prohibited: antenna selection, gain, cable loss, pointing, propagation, or a reference fault can change relative power. Auto-swapping would reverse the declared control and break provenance; only a controlled disconnect or stimulus with retained metadata may close the role-assignment gap.
Why automatic power-based channel swapping is prohibited: relative power can change with antenna, gain, cable loss, pointing, propagation, or a reference-chain fault. It is not a physical role measurement. Swapping roles because one channel is louder would reverse the declared experiment control, destroy provenance, and make later RF or aircraft analysis ambiguous. Channel role is fixed by recorded physical evidence, not inferred from IQ amplitude. CTRL-001

Receiver state is incompletely recorded. The G2 acquisition audit found 18 of 21 required items. Explicit overrun/drop counters, explicit lock status, and a channel-mapping-verification capture were missing. Header readback is valuable but does not cover these omissions.
GPS and ADS-B readiness are separate questions. ADS-B files are packaged historically, while the GPS/NMEA logger is not shown in the sampled manifests. V5: the Pi that timestamps ADS-B was 14.9 s slow before 2026-09-25 21:07 UTC; it now keeps time from internet NTP (accepted, 0.1 s tolerance), and its GPS/PPS reference is still not locked (section 5A). The future readiness plan also requires gzip integrity, temporal coverage, cadence, velocity availability, and geometry checks before ADS-B can support a qualified opportunity.
RF configuration is evolving. Historical manifests, current coordinator defaults, and the proposed field baseline are not identical. Future work must version and validate the exact center frequency, LO offset, gain, antenna ports, semantic roles, and physical antenna/cable identity for every accepted package.
Collection suitability remains unclosed. A collection-suitability decision requires the upstream hardware/ADS-B gates and a reviewed timing/geometry policy. It cannot be inferred from a successful IQ readback, a synchronized replay, or a visually plausible passive map.

Primary evidence: S09 G2 Stage 1, S09 G2 Stage 2, S07 controlled readiness plan, and S08 provenance plan.

10. Meaning and limits of the infrastructure evidence

Bottom line (ELI5): This report proves that the project has collection infrastructure and a growing reproducibility chain. It does not prove that an aircraft echo is found, that a track is correct, or that an aircraft can be localized.

This report establishes:
  • receiver-side deployment and collection-support hardware exist;
  • dual-channel IQ capture and independent ADS-B collection are implemented;
  • historical sessions were packaged with manifest, settings/readback, ADS-B, and logs;
  • a named baseline can be ingested, replayed, and digitally aligned under a documented diagnostic contract;
  • specific field-readiness gaps are known and traceable.
This report does not establish:
  • live-aircraft detection or a validated passive range-Doppler measurement;
  • operational Pd, operational Pfa, detection range, or surveillance coverage;
  • aircraft tracking or track-to-truth quality;
  • localization accuracy or localization capability;
  • reference-chain sufficiency, full receiver lock, or field-qualified collection suitability.

11. What Engineering Capability Exists Today?

Bottom line (ELI5): If the project ended today, it would leave behind a real collection capability and a much better starting point for the next experiment: installed infrastructure, coordinated data capture, independent truth logging, evidence packages, and replayable analysis inputs.

Recommended Management Interpretation

Demonstrated

  • Physical deployment
  • Coordinated collection
  • Replayability
  • Digital synchronization capability

Not Yet Established

  • Reference-chain adequacy
  • Collection suitability
  • Aircraft measurement generation

Next Required Evidence

  • Channel-role verification
  • Reference-path qualification
  • Lock and dropped-sample evidence
  • Collection-suitability approval

Promotion blockers in rank order

  1. Reference-path adequacy. This is the first promotion blocker because the accepted Reference Path was 9.969 dB weaker than the Surveillance Path in the saved baseline. The A-B-A test must establish reference quality without turning a power observation into a role decision. RF-002; CTRL-001
  2. Channel-role verification. Every later RF, synchronization, or measurement interpretation depends on knowing which physical path generated each channel. Controlled physical verification must replace the historical manual mapping caveat. PH-004; CTRL-001
  3. Lock and drop/overrun recording. A future IQ file is not trustworthy enough for promotion unless the package records radio lock, requested/readback agreement, and zero dropped/overflow evidence. CTRL-001
  4. Collection-suitability acceptance. The project needs a reviewed PASS/HOLD decision that joins RF, timing, ADS-B coverage, package integrity, and configuration evidence before a collection is counted as qualified. CTRL-001
  5. Configuration freeze. The intended baseline must be versioned and executed as one controlled configuration; otherwise the 540 MHz/200 kHz development default can be conflated with the 599 MHz/0 Hz field baseline. CFG-001; CTRL-001

Why this work matters

Physical capability

A field receiver installation exists: antenna supports, cables/conduit, enclosure, labelled RF roles, auxiliary SDR hardware, and an operator station. That equipment can be inspected and improved rather than rebuilt from a concept.

Repeatable collection capability

Coordinated IQ and ADS-B collection produces named packages with configuration/readback metadata, IQ file lists, logs, and truth artifacts. A later team can examine the same package.

Evidence capability

G1/G2/G3 convert a saved package into decode, RF-health, and synchronization evidence. They expose weaknesses instead of concealing them, which is essential for the next field campaign.

For a technical manager, the infrastructure value is durable. It reduces the risk that each future result depends on a one-off workstation state or undocumented rooftop configuration. It supports repeatable experimentation because a collection can be named, packaged, moved, reopened, checked against recorded settings, and challenged by later reviewers. It also makes limitations productive: the field gates now specify exactly which evidence is missing instead of allowing a vague “hardware issue” to obscure the next action.

The sensible next investment is therefore not a presentation of downstream radar performance. It is the smallest controlled field-readiness push that proves the reference chain, port/role identity, N320 lock/readback/drop state, ADS-B coverage, and complete package integrity for an accepted collection. Once those inputs are trustworthy, later G1–G4 and detector work can be evaluated on a sound foundation.

Primary evidence: S07 field-readiness acceptance plan, S08 proposed program provenance, and current downstream evidence boundaries.

13. Hardware and collection glossary

Bottom line (ELI5): These terms describe evidence objects and physical paths. They should not be read as automatic proof of radar performance.

ADS-B
Aircraft transponder reports containing identity/position/velocity information. In this project it is independent post-hoc truth/geometry context, not a replacement for a radar measurement.
Baseband IQ
Complex in-phase and quadrature radio samples retained by the receiver. The dual-channel files are the raw material for later passive-bistatic processing.
Reference Path (RF1:RX2 → channel 2)
The declared receiver path intended to contain a usable copy of the HDTV broadcast. It anchors later cancellation and alignment; its adequacy and physical mapping must be demonstrated, not inferred from power.
Surveillance Path (RF0:RX2 → channel 1)
The declared receiver path intended to observe the scene plus the broadcast signal, including any reflected components of interest. It is the fixed control in the proposed A-B-A reference-chain experiment.
Channel-role verification
Physical evidence tying a named RF connector, capture-channel order, antenna/cable path, and manifest metadata to the declared Reference Path or Surveillance Path. Relative power alone is not verification.
USRP N320
The dual-channel software-defined radio used for the documented IQ capture path.
Header readback
Metadata read from a written baseband file—such as center frequency, sample rate, LO offset, and recording time—to compare what was requested with what the file records.
Session ID
A shared unique label tying together capture files, ADS-B collection, logs, manifest, and later analysis.
Session manifest
A structured packing list for a collection. It records paths, timing, configuration, and related artifacts; its schema determines what can later be verified.
Provenance
The chain of evidence that explains where an artifact came from, which configuration produced it, and how a reviewer can repeat or challenge the result.
Replay
Reopening saved artifacts in a controlled analysis path without rerunning rooftop hardware. A replay proves something about the saved package, not all future field sessions.
PPS
Pulse-per-second timing signal. The hardware/logging infrastructure supports timing work, but this report does not claim a verified PPS-disciplined receiver capture.
Collection suitability
A decision that a package has enough verified hardware state, integrity, timing, truth coverage, and RF quality for its intended downstream use.
